meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 15: Talking about Preferences: I Like Japanese Anime

items.note: な-adjective. Takes な before a following noun (e.g. すきな アニメ, "favorite anime"), but です directly after it when it's the sentence's predicate, as in ...が すきです.
ます-form of かく (kaku, "draw"); かく is the dictionary form, used in casual speech and before grammar patterns like のが すきです.
Attaches to a verb's dictionary form to turn it into a noun-equivalent, so it can be followed by が すきです like a noun would (e.g. サッカーを みるのが すきです, "like watching soccer"). See GRAMMAR 3.
items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 1: Meeting: Nice to Meet You (matched on target)

items.note: な-adjective. Almost always used to describe OTHER people, not yourself or your own family, because it sounds like boasting to say it about yourself; people rarely ask じょうずですか ("are you good at...?") for this reason.

items.english: What kind of anime do you like?
items.note: どんな + noun + が すきですか asks what someone likes from within a specific category (here, which kind of anime).
items.target: どんなアニメがすきですか

items.note: Short for わたしも ロボットの アニメが すきです ("I like mecha anime too"). わたしもです is used to say "I am the same as the previous speaker," whether the original statement was affirmative or negative.
Demonstrates person は noun が すきです ("X likes Y").
items.target: チャンさんはワインがすきです

items.note: Demonstrates person は noun が じょうずです ("X is good at Y"). じょうずです is normally used only to describe other people, not yourself.
items.target: チャンさんはにほんごがじょうずです

items.note: Demonstrates person は verb [dictionary form] のが すきです ("X likes doing Y"); の turns the dictionary-form verb みる into a noun-equivalent so it can take が すきです.
items.target: スミスさんはサッカーをみるのがすきです

items.note: Regular 2 verb, introduced directly in dictionary form (Regular 2 verbs from this lesson onward are listed this way rather than as ます-form).
ます-form is ききます (kikimasu).
items.reviewNote: From the WORD POWER "Dictionary form" illustration (Page_145_Image_0001.jpg), which pairs ききます・きく with no English gloss given anywhere in the chapter; the "listen, hear" meaning is inferred from general vocabulary, not confirmed by the source text.

items.note: Negative present form of すきです (suki desu, "like"). Demonstrated in context in Exercise II: かとうさんは コーヒーが すきじゃありません ("Kato-san doesn't like coffee").
Past affirmative form of すきです (suki desu, "like").
Past negative form of すきです (suki desu, "like").
items.target: すきじゃありませんでした

items.note: Negative present form of じょうずです (jouzu desu, "be good at"). Demonstrated in context: テニスが じょうずじゃありません ("not good at tennis", Exercise II) and サッカーが すきです。でも、じょうずじゃありません ("I like soccer, but I'm not good at it", Speaking Practice).
items.target: じょうずじゃありません

items.note: Past affirmative form of じょうずです (jouzu desu, "be good at").
Past negative form of じょうずです (jouzu desu, "be good at").
items.target: じょうずじゃありませんでした

items.reviewNote: Exercise I's conjugation chart (Page_146_Image_0001.jpg) teaches the past-tense forms でした / じゃありませんでした for すきです / じょうずです, but no sentence anywhere in the chapter's text actually uses them. This reuses チャンさん and にほんご from Key Sentence 2 to demonstrate じょうずでした in context.
items.target: チャンさんはにほんごがじょうずでした

items.english: Kato-san likes Japanese sake. He is good at golf.
items.note: Exercise II's worked example for stating what someone likes and is skilled at, combining grammar points 1's two patterns in one exchange.
items.reviewNote: にほんしゅ (nihonshu, "Japanese sake") is not glossed in any VOCABULARY box in this chapter; it appears only as part of this exercise's own worked example.
items.target: かとうさんはにほんしゅがすきです。ゴルフがじょうずです

items.english: Kato-san doesn't like coffee. He is not good at tennis.
items.note: Exercise II's worked example for stating what someone dislikes and is unskilled at.
items.target: かとうさんはコーヒーがすきじゃありません。テニスがじょうずじゃありません

items.note: Exercise III's worked example for asking someone whether they like something.
items.target: すずきさんはスポーツがすきですか

items.note: Dictionary form of はなします (hanashimasu, "talk, speak"); Regular 1 verbs change the sound before ます to form the dictionary form.
items.reviewNote: From Exercise IV's verb-conjugation reference chart (Page_148_Image_0001.jpg).

items.note: Dictionary form of うたいます (utaimasu, "sing"). Used in context in Exercise VII: うたうのも すきです ("I also like singing").
items.reviewNote: From Exercise IV's verb-conjugation reference chart (Page_148_Image_0001.jpg).

items.note: Dictionary form of およぎます (oyogimasu, "swim").
items.reviewNote: From Exercise IV's verb-conjugation reference chart (Page_148_Image_0001.jpg).

items.note: Dictionary form of はしります (hashirimasu, "run").
items.reviewNote: From Exercise IV's verb-conjugation reference chart (Page_148_Image_0001.jpg).

items.note: Dictionary form of たべます (tabemasu, "eat"); Regular 2 verbs form the dictionary form by changing ます to る.
items.reviewNote: Exercise V's own worked example for the "change to dictionary form" drill (たべます → たべる).

items.note: イタリア (Italy) + りょうり (food, cooking, cuisine).
Base word behind the compound イタリアりょうり ("Italian cuisine"): イタリア (Italy) + りょうり.

items.english: Do you like listening to music, Green-san?
items.note: Exercise VII's worked example for talking about what you like to do.
items.target: グリーンさんはおんがくをきくのがすきですか

items.english: Yes, I do. What about you, Kato-san?
items.scene: replying to whether he likes listening to music, then turning the question back to the other speaker
items.note: 「Xさんは?」on its own is a common way to turn a question back on someone: "What about X?"
items.target: ええ、すきです。かとうさんは?

items.english: I like it too. I also like singing.
items.scene: replying that he also likes listening to music
items.note: うたうのも すきです extends the person は verb[dictionary form] のが すきです pattern with も ("also, too") in place of が.
items.target: わたしもすきです。うたうのもすきです

items.reviewNote: Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 3: Asking the Time: What Time Is It? (matched on english)
Possibly already taught — already introduced in Lesson 8: Doing Things (1): I’m Going to Eat Tempura (matched on target)

items.english: I like soccer. But I'm not good at it.
items.reviewNote: The only sentence in the chapter using でも ("but"); extracted from the SPEAKING PRACTICE dialogue under the dialogue exception, since でも is glossed as chapter vocabulary but demonstrated nowhere else.
items.target: サッカーがすきです。でも、じょうずじゃありません

items.note: See サッカーが すきです。でも、じょうずじゃありません。 ("I like soccer, but I'm not good at it.")
